questions.text:
The following are some events that occur after a device controller issues an interrupt while process L is under execution.
(P) The processor pushes the process status of L onto the control stack.
(Q) The processor finishes the execution of the current instruction.
(R) The processor executes the interrupt service routine.
(S) The processor pops the process status of L from the control stack.
(T) The processor loads the new PC value based on the interrupt.
Which one of the following is the correct order in which the events above occur?
questions.solution:
Order of interrupt handling:
Q: finish the current instruction [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P: save L's status on the stack [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T: load the PC with the ISR address [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R: run the ISR [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S: restore L's status.

Answer: QPTRS

questions.text:
Consider the following processor design characteristics.
I. Register-to-register arithmetic operations only
II. Fixed-length instruction format
III. Hardwired control unit
Which of the characteristics above are used in the design of a RISC processor?
questions.solution:
RISC processors use load/store architecture (arithmetic only between registers), fixed-length instructions for easy decoding, and a fast hardwired control unit. All three apply.

Answer: I, II and III

questions.text: A cache memory needs an access time of 30 ns and main memory 150 ns, what is average access time of CPU (assume hit ratio = 80%)?
questions.solution:
Taking the cache first, then main memory on a miss:
[latex]0.8\times30+0.2\times(30+150)=24+36=60[/latex] ns

Answer: 60 ns

questions.text: Which interrupt in 8085 Microprocessor is unmaskable?
questions.solution:
In the 8085, TRAP is the non-maskable interrupt (highest priority). RST 7.5, 6.5 and 5.5 can be masked.

Answer: TRAP
